anderson_darling_normal.doc: Anderson-Darling test for normality. A² = -n - (1/n) * Σ (2i-1)[ln(Φ(z_i)) + ln(1-Φ(z_{n+1-i}))] Modified statistic: A²* = A²(1 + 0.75/n + 2.25/n²) Critical values: 0.631 (15%), 0.752 (10%), 0.873 (5%), 1.035 (2.5%), 1.159 (1%)
anderson_darling_normal.name: anderson_darling_normal

chi_squared_test.doc: Chi-squared goodness-of-fit test. χ² = Σ (O_i - E_i)² / E_i df = k - 1 where k is the number of categories.
chi_squared_test.name: chi_squared_test

ks_test_2sample.doc: Two-sample Kolmogorov-Smirnov test. Tests if two samples come from the same distribution. KS statistic = max |F1(x) - F2(x)| over all x.
ks_test_2sample.name: ks_test_2sample

ks_test_normal.doc: One-sample KS test against normal distribution. Tests if sample comes from N(sample_mean, sample_std).
ks_test_normal.name: ks_test_normal

pearson_r.doc: Pearson correlation coefficient and p-value. Returns CorrResult(r, p_value). p-value uses the t-distribution: t = r * sqrt(n-2) / sqrt(1-r²), df = n-2
pearson_r.name: pearson_r

pearson_r_strict.doc: `pearson_r`, but NaN/±Inf in `x` or `y` raises instead of returning `CorrResult(NaN, NaN)`.
pearson_r_strict.name: pearson_r_strict

shapiro_wilk_approx.doc: Approximate Shapiro-Wilk test for normality (for n <= 5000). Uses a simplified version based on the correlation between sample order statistics and expected normal order statistics. W ≈ (Σ a_i * x_(i))² / Σ(x_i - x̄)² For large n, we approximate a_i using normal quantiles.
shapiro_wilk_approx.name: shapiro_wilk_approx

spearman_r.doc: Spearman rank correlation coefficient and p-value. Returns CorrResult(rho, p_value). Ranks ties by averaging. P-value uses the t-distribution approximation.
spearman_r.name: spearman_r

spearman_r_strict.doc: `spearman_r`, but NaN/±Inf in `x` or `y` raises instead of returning `CorrResult(NaN, NaN)`.
spearman_r_strict.name: spearman_r_strict

t_test_1sample.name: t_test_1sample

t_test_2sample.doc: Two-sample (independent) t-test: test if means are equal. Uses Welch's t-test (unequal variances). t = (x̄₁ - x̄₂) / √(s₁²/n₁ + s₂²/n₂) df from Welch-Satterthwaite equation.
t_test_2sample.name: t_test_2sample

compute_std_from_values.name: compute_std_from_values

part3.doc: Median-of-3 partition of `a[lo..hi]`, returning the pivot's final index.

pctile.name: pctile

percentile.doc: Linear-interpolated percentile of UNSORTED input, p in [0,100].
